title: Investigate Taskfold IPC overflow and extraction options

goals.text: Investigate Taskfold IPC and extraction options, and establish pig-taskfolding with architecture, specifications, research, evaluations, UX designs, and implementation plans without host-side fixes.

pins.text: we do not need a web interface but it must be performant
we cannot fix the host side without forking pig, so this is out.

report.outcome: Located local PiG IPC implementation, Accordion turn_end hook, and tree-navigator sources; crash stderr file exists but is empty. Scope is investigation and architecture recommendations, with no implementation changes.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Locate relevant runtime, Taskfold and navigator sources.

tasks.title: Investigate the oversized turn_end IPC payload and whether Taskfold causes the frame-limit overflow.

report.outcome: Traced frame rejection to PiG event dispatch and identified full boundary context serialization with repeated history representations; Accordion's turn_end handler itself only emits a turn/revision notification. Exact offending session and field sizes remain unavailable, so Taskfold causation is not established.
open: No incident reproduction: supplied stderr log is empty and affected session was not identified.
Need field-size measurements of the actual turn_end event and installed host revision.

tasks.title: Evaluate pi-tree-navigator ideas: each fold as a branch or separate session, plus resume and tree-view patches.

report.outcome: Tree-navigator uses same-session rewind plus summary and retained original subtree, not a session per fold. Its prepare/summarize/validated-commit and queued safe-boundary pattern is useful, but branch navigation is not equivalent to selectively unfolding nested task spans.
decisions: Prefer same-session archived spans or branches over one session per fold — avoids session proliferation and task-binding duplication.
Reuse navigation UX concepts, not prototype patches without checking PiG native contracts.

tasks.title: Evaluate extracting all taskfolding into ../pig-taskfolding as a targeted extension with an event API, considering Go or Rust and preserving /tasks, renaming, and centering.

report.outcome: Recommend a focused Go factory extension with task state, reversible span projection and native TUI, but only after addressing PiG's oversized boundary transport. Extraction must include task session binding, notices, anchors, verdicts, recall/unfold and views rather than just the conductor.
decisions: Go over Rust — best-supported factory integration; no measured CPU bottleneck justifies Rust.
Versioned bounded event deltas and paged explicit reads — never publish full session snapshots per task event.
Retain one authoritative task store and host-owned session projection; no web server or browser dependencies.
open: Exact incident payload and installed host revision remain unverified; no reproduction or implementation was performed.

tasks.title: Create the pig-taskfolding repository and its .project/artifacts directory.

report.outcome: Created a new local git repository at /mnt/Projects/furbyhaxx/pig-taskfolding with README, steering, .project template, Justfile and the portable artifact checker. No remote or runtime scaffold was created; artifact content and initial commit follow in task 6.

tasks.title: Produce pig-taskfolding documentation covering specifications for the different parts, architecture, mechanisms, evaluations, designs/wireframes/UX, plans, research, and analyses.

report.outcome: Delivered a committed design-stage pig-taskfolding repository with seven component specs, architecture, lifecycle/folding/event/persistence mechanisms, evaluation gates, terminal wireframes, topology tradeoffs, source evidence, IPC analysis and an executable sliced plan. The no-host-fork constraint is explicit throughout.
decisions: Backend selection remains evidence-gated — no safe live-commit or bounded transport behavior is invented.
Use standard typed .project directories rather than a catch-all artifacts directory.
Local design repository only — no runtime, remote repository or publication.
open: Installed-host feasibility, topology choice, UX approval and measured performance remain future work; optional paid evaluations require authorization.

subtasks.title: Ground host compatibility and topology alternatives in local sources

report.outcome: Recorded local source revisions, SDK candidates and evidence limits; created IPC analysis, no-fork feasibility research and task/session topology alternatives. Live mutation, bounded reads and native resume/tree customization remain explicit probe gates rather than assumed APIs.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Record source revisions, evidence and unresolved compatibility gates.

Contracts cover lifecycle, reversible spans, bounded events, crash recovery, migration, no-fork backend gates and measurable evaluation budgets; no runtime behavior is claimed implemented.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Cover task contracts, folding, events, persistence, UX and measurable acceptance.

subtasks.title: Implement bounded recall (index, page, query) in core and tool

report.outcome: Added core/recallView.ts: recall returns a small fold whole, otherwise an index of subtask codes and code.N entries with previews; code.N reads one entry (paged), query returns addressed excerpts; all bounded by one per-call budget, dedupes members matched via several carriers. Tool in extension/accordion.ts now takes codes/query/page, broadcasts only shown ids, and stores small details.
decisions: 32k-char (~8k tok) per-call budget, constant RECALL_BUDGET_CHARS — no config surface until needed
Pages sized against the full budget regardless of call composition so page N is stable
details carry counts only — the old details duplicated the full text into the persisted session
open: unfold can still restore an arbitrarily large fold into standing context; not guarded
Open tasks still cannot be folded below task granularity (the 768k saturation)

acceptanceCriteria.text: Recall result never exceeds byte budget; large folds return an index with drill-down

tasks.title: Fold finished steps inside open Taskfold tasks so one open task cannot saturate the context

report.outcome: Taskfold now folds old finished steps of open tasks under pressure into recallable step carriers absorbed by the task's record on finish; saturation only remains when nothing foldable exists (commit 9b8fed0 on fix/bounded-recall).
open: Not exercised in a live Pi session; branch not merged/pushed
unfold still has no size ceiling

subtasks.title: Analyze saturation path, span scan and group constraints in taskfold.ts

report.outcome: Saturation fires in evaluate() when plan() under pressure returns nothing; open-task blocks are only reachable via opt-in `floor` (off by default), untracked() skips coverage.open, and unit() treats any non-child group as foreign.
decisions: Generalize untracked() run-grouping into a shared run folder; add open-task scope with a `steps` carrier — reuses proven group-shape logic
unit() absorbs a finishing span's own steps carriers like child records — so a later finish still yields one record

acceptanceCriteria.text: Saturation trigger, foldable units inside open spans and Truth group limits identified

subtasks.title: Implement step folding inside open tasks

report.outcome: Added `steps` pressure pass: foldRuns() shared with untracked() groups old finished steps per innermost open task into `{steps,label,count,changed,verified}` carriers; unit() absorbs those carriers when the task finishes; settings `taskfold.steps` plumbed. The existing saturation test now folds instead of saturating (expected).
decisions: Steps run after untracked in the pressure ladder — oldest-outside work first, current task last
Task start/resume messages, user messages, doc reads and user tail stay live — keeps task identity and steering visible
minSteps default 4 (untracked 8) — open tasks are the dominant growth source

acceptanceCriteria.text: Under pressure an open task's old finished steps fold into recallable groups; working tail stays live
